## v0.7.2 — Maintenance release

Small reliability fixes on top of v0.7.1. No user-facing feature changes.

- **Offline catalog cache fixed.** The last-good cache of the update and
  support-pack catalogs now persists correctly. Previously the write failed
  silently, so a restart while offline (air-gapped) would drop the cached
  catalogs until the next online refresh.
- **Support-pack metadata corrected.** Published packs now stamp an accurate
  minimum-API-version.

## v0.7.1 — Maintenance release

A small maintenance release on top of v0.7.0. No user-facing feature changes.

- **Database packaging cleanup.** The bundled PostgreSQL 16 service is now named
  consistently across the stack. Existing installs are unaffected; the update
  catalog's database image reference is corrected to `postgres:16.4`.
- **Dashboard internals.** Removed retired per-industry preset code (the
  capability-gated dashboard introduced in v0.7.0 is the sole driver). No change
  to existing dashboards.
- **Support-pack signing key rotated** to `vendor-prod-2026-r2`.

## AI Data Collect v0.7.0

### Database engine: TimescaleDB → PostgreSQL 16
The platform now runs on plain **PostgreSQL 16** instead of TimescaleDB. Event and
report history is stored using native PostgreSQL range partitioning (one partition
per day for events, per month for reports), with an in-app maintenance service that
creates upcoming partitions and prunes data beyond your retention window. This
simplifies the stack and removes a third-party extension while preserving all
existing data and analytics behavior.

> **Upgrading an existing install requires a one-time data migration** (a short
> maintenance window). See `compose/P6-CUTOVER.md` and the automated
> `compose/p6-cutover.sh`. New installs need no action.

### Dashboard & enrollment facelift
- **Capability-aware dashboards** — each camera now carries a capability snapshot;
  dashboard cards for features a camera doesn't support are hidden, and
  supported-but-not-yet-enabled features are clearly marked.
- **Camera support driven by data** — model capability detection corrected and
  moved onto typed, data-driven camera-support profiles.
- **Simplified setup** — the 13 fixed industry templates have been retired in favor
  of the capability-driven dashboard (existing layouts continue to load).

### Under the hood
- Retention and heatmap pruning now run as app-side services on a fixed schedule.
- Analytics time-bucketing reimplemented on native PostgreSQL (`date_bin`),
  byte-for-byte equivalent to the previous output.

## v0.6.0 — Every line, every lens, and your nightly camera reports on the dashboard

This release fills in the rest of the dashboard. Every counting line you draw
now gets its own card, your cameras' nightly statistics reports show up as
cards, and live crowd and slip-&-fall detection are wired through end to end.
It also fixes a batch of quiet failures that could leave a newly added camera
half-configured.

### What's new
- **Each counting line gets its own card.** Draw two lines on the same camera
  and you now get two separate cards — one per line — instead of the two
  collapsing into a single combined count.
- **Your nightly camera reports, as dashboard cards.** The daily statistics
  your cameras already upload (people counting, vehicle counting, queue
  management, crowd counting) can now be added straight to the dashboard as
  trend cards, alongside everything else.
- **Live crowd counting.** Cameras that report crowd levels now feed a Crowd
  Count card that shows the day's peak.
- **Slip-&-fall alerts.** Cameras with slip-&-fall detection now surface a
  Slip & Fall card so you can keep an eye on incidents.
- **Multi-sensor cameras deliver on every lens.** Each lens on a multi-sensor
  camera now reliably reports its own crossings and dwell, so a four-sensor
  camera fills in all four sensors instead of only the first.

### Fixes & polish
- **Reports now load reliably.** Fixed an issue that could stop a camera's
  uploaded reports from being saved, which left report cards empty.
- **Previously used cameras connect cleanly.** Fixed three silent failures
  that could leave a re-used camera stuck on "needs attention" — the live
  events connection, the secure certificate install when a camera's
  certificate store was full, and a misreported report setup step now all
  surface and resolve correctly.
- **Removing a camera leaves nothing behind.** Deleting a camera now fully
  clears its zones, cards, reports, and history so the next camera you add
  starts from a clean slate.

No action is required to upgrade. Existing dashboards keep working, and the
new card types are available immediately from the dashboard.

## v0.5.0 — A guided setup, from a blank screen to live numbers

This release rebuilds the first hour with the product. A fresh install now
opens to a blank dashboard and a single **Set up** button that walks you
through the whole job one camera at a time — add the camera, draw the spots
you care about, turn them into cards — without ever leaving the page or
picking a "role" from a list.

### What's new
- **A guided Setup Wizard.** One button replaces the old scatter of
  "add a camera / add a card / set up a camera / count across cameras"
  options. It walks you camera-by-camera: connect the camera, draw your
  lines and areas, name them in plain words, and the cards appear. When you
  have more than one camera you can add up their entrances into a single
  building headcount at the end.
- **Enter your license key on first run.** New installs can activate online
  by typing the 16-digit key from your welcome email — no offline license
  file required. (The offline file and "activate later" options are still
  there.)
- **Multi-sensor cameras, one lens at a time.** Cameras with several lenses
  (e.g. four-sensor models) now keep each lens separate everywhere — when
  you draw zones, build cards, or add a lens into a headcount group, you pick
  the exact sensor instead of guessing. No more lenses collapsing into one.
- **Cameras come in clean.** Adding a camera no longer pushes pre-drawn
  zones you didn't ask for. If the camera already has zones on it, you choose
  to **use what's there** or **clear and start fresh** — then draw exactly
  what you want.
- **Draw a line, watch the card light up.** A counting line you draw in the
  wizard now feeds its dashboard card directly. You pick which way is "coming
  in" as you draw, and the card fills in with the last 7 days of crossings.
- **Pick what an area measures.** When you set up an area you choose how to
  measure it instead of being given one fixed answer.

### Fixes & polish
- Building a card or a group no longer creates duplicates if you set the same
  one up twice — the wizard recognizes what's already there.
- Leaving the dashboard with unsaved changes now warns you first.
- The "add up entrances" option only appears once you actually have two or
  more entrances to add up.
- Quieter logs and lighter background polling on a fresh install.

No action is required to upgrade. Existing dashboards keep working; the new
Setup Wizard is available immediately from the dashboard toolbar.

## v0.4.0 — Set up your dashboard in seconds

Turning a camera into a useful dashboard used to mean leaving the page for the Zone Manager, hunting for a drawn area, and tagging it with a fixed role from a long list. This release replaces all of that with a guided, on-dashboard setup wizard — you name the spots you care about in your own words, and the cards light up in seconds.

### What's new
- **"Set up this card."** A card with no data now opens a focused wizard right on the dashboard. Pick the view, choose (or draw) the spot, give it a name in your own words, and Apply — the card fills in with the last 7 days of numbers immediately. No navigating away, no jargon.
- **Name it, don't classify it.** You type a plain name (e.g. "Front Entrance", "Pharmacy Pickup", "Drive-Thru Lane") and it becomes the card title. What the card measures is inferred from what you marked — a **line** counts people crossing, an **area** measures time spent there. You never have to pick a "role."
- **Draw a new spot in the wizard.** If nothing is marked on a view yet, draw a box or a line right in the setup window — it's saved to the camera and the card starts watching it.
- **"Set up this camera."** For a multi-lens camera, set up everything in one pass: every area and line across all of its lenses is listed, you check the ones you want, name them, and Apply builds all the cards at once.
- **Build-your-own dashboards.** Start from a blank dashboard and add exactly the cards you want with **"Add a card."** Save it as your own named dashboard.
- **Count across cameras.** A new **"Count across cameras"** card adds up several entrances into one live building headcount — point it at an existing camera group or create one right from the dashboard.

### Fixes
- **Saved dashboards now reliably survive a reload.** A storage issue could cause custom cards, saved layouts, and per-card filters to be dropped when the page reloaded; saved dashboards are now persisted correctly. (Layouts saved before upgrading may need to be saved once more.)

No action is required. Existing dashboards keep working, and the new setup wizard is available immediately on any card that doesn't have data yet.

## v0.3.2 — Multi-sensor lens analytics

Multi-sensor cameras (such as 4-lens Hanwha PNM-C models) are now first-class on the dashboard. Previously a multi-sensor appeared as a single opaque camera, and per-lens zones that shared a name could be mis-attributed to the wrong role.

### What's new
- **Per-lens analytics.** Events now carry which camera lens (sensor) they came from, so each lens's zones, roles, and metrics are tracked independently. A multi-sensor that reuses the same zone name across lenses no longer collapses them into one.
- **New Multi-Sensor view.** A dedicated page (sidebar → **Multi-Sensor**) shows each lens of a multi-sensor camera side by side — its zone map (with roles) and an activity chart scoped to just that lens.
- **Lens-aware dashboard cards.** A dashboard card's source selector now expands a multi-sensor camera into its individual lenses, so you can scope a tile to one sensor.

### Fixes
- A dashboard card's camera/lens + time-window selection now **saves immediately and survives a refresh** — previously a change could silently revert.
- Zone-role tiles (e.g. **Entrance Flow**) on a multi-sensor camera now show the correct data instead of appearing empty.

No action is required. Existing dashboards keep working and single-sensor cameras are unaffected; per-lens history for multi-sensor cameras rebuilds automatically after the upgrade.

## AI Data Collect v0.3.1

### Multi-sensor camera zone management
Cameras with more than one image sensor — such as the Hanwha PNM-C multi-sensor
series — now have a **Sensor** selector in Zone Manager. Each sensor shows its own
live snapshot and its own detection zones and lines, so you can view, draw, rename,
and assign roles to zones on every lens, not just the first. Single-sensor cameras
are unchanged.

### Camera support, streamlined
- Event normalization (how incoming camera events are mapped to analytics types)
  now ships as part of the signed camera-support data, so new camera families can
  be added through a support-pack update rather than an application release.
- Internal reliability and maintenance improvements to camera enrollment.

## v0.3.0 — Shippable camera support, multi-sensor enrollment & network survey

This release turns camera support into **installable, signed data** that can grow without an app update, rounds out enrollment for multi-sensor and specialized cameras, and adds a one-click **network survey** that reports exactly which cameras on a subnet are supported.

### What's new

- **Camera support as installable packs** — Support for new camera models now ships as a signed *support pack* (data, not code). Installing a pack takes effect immediately — no application restart — so newly tested cameras become enrollable without waiting for a release.
- **Online pack catalog + "pending device support" queue** — The system can check a signed online catalog for new support packs and install them in one click (fully optional and air-gap-safe — offline systems simply skip it). Cameras the wizard can't yet fully support are added to a pending-support queue that auto-clears when a matching pack arrives.
- **Camera "personalities"** — Cameras running a specialized on-camera AI app (for example a factory & safety app that detects *Person + Forklift*) are now recognized and configured with the right object vocabulary automatically, labeled by their role.
- **Multi-sensor cameras** — Multi-lens cameras (e.g. multi-directional / multi-sensor models) now have **every sensor configured**, not just the first channel. Each lens is read and configured against its own capability.
- **Smarter zone takeover** — Adopting a camera's existing zones now suggests a role for each zone from its name (editable), so taking over a pre-configured camera lands closer to ready.
- **Warehouse & logistics analytics** — New Forklift and Vehicle activity tiles and a Logistics/Warehouse dashboard template surface object-class activity alongside the existing people-centric metrics.
- **Network survey** — A new **Survey network** page scans a private subnet, identifies every camera, and reports support coverage at a glance (verified / supported / refused / unidentified) with model, firmware, and analytics path per device. Export the report as CSV or JSON — ideal for site audits and pre-deployment planning.

### Notes
- Standard single-sensor cameras enroll exactly as before; the new behavior applies only where it's relevant (multi-sensor hardware, app-specific cameras, takeover).
- The online pack catalog is optional and never degrades an offline or air-gapped install — it fails closed and quietly.
- No configuration changes are required after upgrading.

## v0.2.9 — Smarter, capability-aware camera enrollment

This release teaches enrollment to **read each camera's real analytics capability and configure only what it supports**, instead of assuming a fixed object list and pushing it. The result: specialized cameras (warehouse/factory AI apps, motion-only models, FTP-only families) enroll cleanly instead of throwing rejected-analytics errors, and cameras you're taking over keep their existing setup.

### What's new
- **Capability-driven analytics** — During configuration we now read the camera's advertised + currently-configured object types and reconcile them with our defaults. We never send an object type the camera rejects, so analytics no longer fails on cameras whose AI vocabulary differs from the standard retail set (e.g. a warehouse camera that detects *Person + Forklift* but not vehicles).
- **"Adopt existing zones" (takeover-friendly)** — Keeping a camera's zones now preserves its purpose-built configuration and simply enables event delivery using the object types it already supports. We never overwrite zones unless you explicitly choose "Replace."
- **Expanded analytics vocabulary** — Forklift, vehicle subtypes (car/bus/truck/…), and license-plate events are now labeled consistently in the event stream.
- **Clearer health signals** — A camera whose analytics only partially configured now flags for attention instead of reading "healthy." Report transport (SFTP vs FTP) is labeled accurately, and the live-events connection shows the correct secure MQTTS port.
- **Better device support requests** — "Request device support" now captures a read-only device fingerprint (model, on-camera apps, supported object types, transports) so unsupported or edge cameras can be added to the support library faster.

### Notes
- Standard cameras enroll exactly as before — the reconcile is transparent when a camera supports the full default set.
- No configuration changes are required; the smarter behavior applies automatically on your next enrollment or re-configure.

## What's new

**Click any chart widget to enlarge it.** Tap a module on your dashboard and it opens full-size in a clean window — a big, easy-to-read chart up top with the underlying events listed right below it. Scroll through the records and export them to CSV without ever leaving the view. Press Esc or click away to return.

**Color-coded trends at a glance.** Charts now highlight what matters. Time-sensitive measures like wait times, queue depth, and after-hours activity shade green / amber / red against sensible thresholds, while volume measures like traffic and occupancy spotlight their busiest days. Quiet, normal days stay calm so the exceptions jump out.

**Smarter chart shapes.** A long daily range now draws as a single continuous trend line that fits the whole window on one screen — no more scrolling a wall of skinny bars to read a year. Shorter ranges and the monthly roll-up still use bars, and notable days are marked with a standout dot.

## What's new

**Make the dashboard yours — now fully editable.** A new Edit mode lets you drag widgets to rearrange them, hide or remove the ones you don't need, and reset to the default layout anytime. Nothing saves until you say so: keep several named layouts, switch between them, and rename or delete them as your needs change.

**Per-widget time and camera filters.** Each widget now carries its own time range and camera scope, shown as a chip in its header — so you can put "last 7 days at the front entrance" right next to "this year across all cameras" on the same screen. A caption under each title spells out exactly what you're looking at.

**See your busiest cameras at a glance.** A new "Most Active Cameras" widget ranks your cameras by activity over any time range.

**Clearer trend charts.** Charts now label their axis intelligently — weekdays, month names, or dates depending on the span — and a Day/Month toggle rolls a long range up into monthly bars. **A more focused home screen.** Camera Groups moved to the bottom of the dashboard and appear only once you've created one. System Health's alerts now match the 24-hour window shown on its tile.

## What's new

**A redesigned, customizable dashboard.** Your home screen now leads with your camera data. Build the view you want: add and arrange widgets from a gallery, save multiple layouts, and switch between them. On first run after adding a camera, a layout picker offers 12 ready-made templates (including a General template for any setup) to get you started in one click.

## v0.2.5 — Camera enrollment reliability fixes

No configuration changes and no action required. Existing installs can apply this from the in-product **Updates** page.

### Fixes
- **Enrolling a camera with a saved credential now reports "Connected" correctly.** When you picked an existing saved credential during enrollment (instead of typing the password again), the camera-status check ran without the password and the camera answered with an authorization error — so the wizard kept showing a yellow "checking / not connected" state even though the camera was actually enrolled and streaming events. The status check now resolves the saved credential the same way enrollment does, so the camera shows as connected as soon as it is.
- **The final enrollment screen now waits for secure (MQTTS) cameras to finish connecting.** Secure-MQTT cameras can take longer than the previous one-time check allowed to complete their handshake, which could leave the screen showing a false "not connected" warning until you manually refreshed. The screen now watches the camera's status for a short period after enrollment and updates on its own once the camera connects. Status can only improve during this window — a camera that is mid-handshake is never shown as failed.
- **Report-upload (FTP/SFTP) configuration is validated correctly on cameras that only support plain FTP.** Some camera models accept a "configure" request at the protocol level but reject the secure-transport setting internally. The server now inspects the camera's actual response rather than only the request status, so it no longer reports a secure report connection on a camera that only supports plain FTP. Cameras that only support plain FTP continue to be labeled as such.

_All container images were rebuilt for this release._

## v0.2.4 — Security & MQTTS camera-connection fixes

No configuration changes and no action required. Existing installs can apply this from the in-product **Updates** page.

### Fixes
- **MQTTS cameras now reconnect reliably after a certificate change.** Some cameras (e.g. Hanwha TNV-C8011RW and similar models) could fail to receive an updated trusted-CA certificate when re-enrolled — for example after the server's MQTT certificate authority was regenerated — leaving the camera unable to complete the secure (MQTTS) handshake and silently producing no events. The certificate is now correctly replaced on these cameras, so secure-MQTT enrollment and re-enrollment connect and stream events as expected.
- **Credentials are no longer written to application logs.** Camera request logging could, in some cases, record camera/broker credentials in plaintext in the backend logs. Logging is now clamped and a redaction safeguard strips any credentials (passwords, tokens, keys) from log output. Existing log files are unaffected by this change; only newly written logs benefit.

### Internal
- Added a regression test that locks in the corrected MQTTS certificate-unbind behavior across camera models.

_All container images were rebuilt for this release._

## v0.2.3 — License page redesign & clearer enrollment guardrails

No configuration changes and no action required. Existing installs can apply this from the in-product **Updates** page.

### What's new
- **Redesigned License page.** A cleaner, at-a-glance view of your license: current device usage against your seat count, support-plan status with its expiry date, and a short license reference for support calls (full identifiers are still available under Details). When you're at your seat limit, the page now shows a calm, informational notice rather than an alarming one — being at capacity is a normal state, not an error.
- **Check for Updates, in one place.** The license actions are consolidated, including a clear "Check for Updates" action. On air-gapped installs, online-only actions are hidden automatically.
- **Clearer enrollment limits.** When your license is inactive or at its seat limit, the portal now consistently prevents adding a camera — both on the Devices page and at the very first step of the enrollment wizard — with a plain-language explanation of why. This mirrors the server's existing enforcement, so you find out before you start, not after.

### Fixes
- The License page now shows your **actual** enrolled device count instead of occasionally displaying 0.

### Internal cleanup
- Added automated safeguards that verify every camera-enrollment path stays behind the license check, and resolved a framework deprecation warning. No user-visible change.

_All container images were rebuilt for this release._

## v0.2.2 — Maintenance release

No configuration changes and no action required. Existing installs can apply this from the in-product **Updates** page.

### Improvements
- **Faster license-state propagation.** Activating or removing a license now reflects in event processing within about a minute, instead of taking up to an hour to reach the ingest workers. (The periodic re-verification remains in place as a backstop, so time-based changes such as support-plan expiry are unaffected.)

### Internal cleanup
- Removed legacy licensing code paths now that all field installations use the current (v3) licensing format: the pre-v3 license-blob fallback, the retired trial-issuer key, and obsolete local signing scripts.

_All container images were rebuilt for this release._

## What's new in v0.2.1

- **More reliable license enforcement after upgrades.** License status checks in the event-ingest pipeline now apply consistently whether you're on a fresh install or upgrading from an earlier version. Previously, this check could stay dormant after an in-place upgrade.
- **Simpler, more secure ingest service.** The ingest worker no longer needs direct database credentials — it now reads license status over the internal service API, reducing its access footprint.

## Upgrade notes

- No action required. This upgrade is drop-in.
- Fresh installs and upgrades both pick up the corrected behavior automatically.
- The ingest worker's database environment variables are no longer used and can be ignored; new installs omit them.

## v0.2.0 — Licensing Overhaul (Phase 3 go-live)

This is a major licensing update. License files no longer carry any
customer identity, activation can now be done online with a short key,
and support-plan status governs which upgrades you can install. The
update is delivered the usual way and works on both internet-connected
and air-gapped deployments.

### What's new

- **Online activation.** On a connected deployment you can now activate
  by typing a 16-character license key on the License page — no file
  exchange needed. Offline/air-gapped deployments keep the existing
  download-system-info → receive-license-file flow, auto-selected when
  the licensing server isn't reachable.
- **Automatic daily refresh.** Connected deployments check in once a day
  to pick up renewals, capacity changes, and revocations automatically.
  This is a no-op on air-gapped systems and never downgrades a working
  license when the server is unreachable.
- **Hardware migration request.** Move a license to new hardware from the
  License page. Within your migration allowance it rebinds immediately;
  beyond it, the request is routed to the vendor for approval.
- **Support-plan gating on updates.** Patch releases install on any active
  license. Minor and major upgrades require an active support plan; a
  lapsed plan still runs and still takes patches, and rollbacks are always
  allowed.
- **Privacy: no identity in license files.** License artifacts no longer
  contain customer name or email, so backups, logs, and support
  attachments don't leak identity.
- **Ingest/writes pause on an expired license.** When a license expires,
  event ingest stops within ~60s and the portal goes read-only until a
  valid license is in place. Existing data is untouched.
- **Refreshed License page** with clear Not-activated / Activating /
  Activated states and per-license actions.

### Upgrade notes

- Existing license files keep working — they're still recognized after
  the upgrade. Connected deployments will refresh automatically; if the

## Hotfix for v0.1.31

Fixes a SUP-gate and write-gate false-unblock caught during integration
testing on the lab VM.

### Bug

On any deployment that still carries a legacy `system_config[license_blob]`
row alongside the v0.1.26+ stackable `licenses` table (every existing
deployment), the Phase 3B SUP-gate and Phase 3G write-gate could be
falsely unblocked. The cross-worker coherence path in `check_can_update`
and `check_writes_allowed` read the legacy single-blob row instead of
the stackable aggregate. When the legacy row's SUP date differed from
the stackable aggregate's (e.g. after install/remove of stackable
licenses), the legacy reading won.

Result on lab VM: install of a lapsed-SUP license + removal of originals
left the stackable aggregate at `valid_support_lapsed`, but the legacy
row was unchanged and reported `valid` with future SUP — the SUP-gate
returned `None` (allowed) for every minor/major upgrade attempt.

### Fix

Swap `reverify_cached_blob` → `get_aggregated_state` in both gate
helpers. The aggregate is the stackable-licensing source of truth on
v0.1.26+ and has its own cross-worker coherence via the
`_active_set_fingerprint` md5 over the licenses table.

### Impact

Any v0.1.31 deployment relying on the SUP-gate or write-gate to block
unauthorized operations was effectively unprotected. Patch + minor +
major upgrades all unblocked; portal mutations on expired-demo
unblocked. Phase 3A band policy, cleanup worker, and Phase 3F worker
event-dropping are unaffected — they don't go through the bugged
paths.

### Test coverage

Updated the original unit tests, which had been mocking the wrong
helper (the very layer that caused the bug). Now mock
`get_aggregated_state` instead. Suite stays at 401 passing.

## Licensing overhaul — Phase 3 batch

This release ships the first batch of the ground-up licensing overhaul
locked in v10.36. Customer-side changes only; vendor portal split into
private creator + public verifier lands in a later release.

### What's new

**Support plan semver gate on updates** — minor and major version bumps
now require an active support plan. Patches and rollbacks remain
available regardless of SUP status. Customers see a renewal CTA on the
Updates page when their SUP is lapsed and a minor/major release is
out. Enforced in two layers: the Updates page filter excludes blocked
versions from the catalog, and the install endpoints return HTTP 403
with a structured `sup_required_for_version` body so a hand-rolled
POST still gets gated.

**Lapsed-SUP customers can add cameras within cap** — previously,
lapsed support blocked adding new cameras. Now the device cap is the
gate, not the SUP date. Perpetual licenses stay perpetual.

**Expired demo hard cutoff** — when a demo license's `expires_at`
passes, ingest workers stop processing camera events, the portal goes
read-only (35 mutation endpoints return HTTP 423 Locked), and all
camera configs are preserved. Installing a paid license immediately
resumes operation. No data is destroyed; no migration is needed.

**Dead-state license auto-purge** — rows that have been in a dead
band (wrong_system_id, expired, revoked, invalid_signature) for more
than 30 days are automatically soft-removed by a new cleanup worker
running every 6 hours. Each purge fires an `license_auto_purged`
audit log entry.

### New endpoints

* `GET /api/v1/system/license-block-status` — read-only view of the
  derived block flags (`blocks_ingest`, `blocks_writes`,
  `blocks_add_seat`). Used by the upcoming portal banner UI; available
  to any signed-in user.

### Schema

* `licenses.state_first_observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ` — new column. Stamped
  when a row enters a dead band; cleared on recovery. Drives the
  30-day cleanup grace period. Idempotent ALTER on first boot, no
  downtime.

### Internal architecture

* New `system_config[license_block_status]` JSON row published by the
  api's licensing reverify cycle. Worker containers (db-writer,
  ftp-ingest) poll this row every 60s instead of re-running the
  signature verify pipeline themselves. Fail-open if the row is
  missing or the api is down.

* api: 343 → 401 tests
* db-writer: 13 → 22 tests
* ftp-ingest: 7 → 15 tests

## v0.1.28 — air-gap install correctness fix

### What this fixes

Customers who installed v0.1.27 via the air-gap **Install from file** path
saw the Updates page continue to show **"1 update available · v0.1.27"**
even after a successful install. Two root causes:

- **The MQTT ingest worker wasn't actually getting updated.** The catalog
  used the service name `mqtt-ingest` while the rest of the stack (Docker
  Compose, the api's target selector) calls it `ingest-worker`. The
  install-target diff joins by service name and silently skipped it. The
  fix renames the catalog entry to match.
- **Some images record an "image-id" digest after offline load** rather
  than the registry manifest digest. The Updates page compared the
  recorded digest against the catalog's manifest digest, found a
  mismatch, and reported an update as still pending. Fixed by having
  the post-install version recorder trust the just-installed bundle's
  catalog digest when the local image record is missing the registry
  origin info.

### Who should install this

Anyone who installed v0.1.27. Symptom is purely cosmetic — the rest of
the stack is healthy — but the false-positive warning is annoying.

file** card you used for v0.1.27. After install completes, the warning
will clear and the Updates page will read "Up to date · v0.1.28".

## v0.1.25 — audit-trail completeness for camera lifecycle

### Camera lifecycle now writes audit rows at every transition

The audit log was missing two of the four lifecycle events and
mis-attributing a third:

- **Enrollment** (`POST /api/v1/devices/`) wrote `cameras` and
  `camera_credentials` rows but no audit row, so compliance reviews
  had to infer "who enrolled this camera" from the `cameras` row's
  `registered_at` alone — with no operator attribution.
- **Restore from trash** wrote an audit row, but hardcoded
  `actor_username="system"` even though restore is an operator
  action gated by `manage_devices` permission. A malicious or
  accidental restore looked like a background event.
- **24-hour auto-purge sweep** (`HealthService._purge_trashed_cameras`)
  silently hard-DELETEd rows once the restore window expired, so
  the audit trail terminated at `camera_deleted` and never recorded
  the row leaving the table.

v0.1.25 fixes all three. The camera lifecycle now reads cleanly
end-to-end in the audit log:

| Stage | Action | Actor |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Wizard enroll | `camera_registered` (new) | operator |
| Portal soft-delete | `camera_deleted` | operator |
| Portal restore | `camera_restored` | operator (was "system") |
| 24h+ auto-purge | `camera_auto_purged` (new) | system (correctly — no operator) |

Detail JSON on each row carries the relevant context — `friendly_name`,
`ip_address`, `manufacturer`, `model`, the symmetric teardown summary
on delete, the re-enable summary on restore, the `trashed_at` delta
on auto-purge. Sufficient for compliance review without joining other
tables.

### First-run.sh: clean up `/var/lib/aidatacollect/{backups,snapshots}` ownership

Cosmetic follow-on to the v0.1.23 Bug E parent-dir chown. The
`backups` and `snapshots` subdirectories used to land as root:root
0777 because docker auto-creates bind-mount targets with that
default. Worked because 0777 made them world-writable, but the
ownership mismatch was ugly and the same trap-class that bit
SFTPGo home_dir (Bug B) and the api state dir (Bug E). first-run.sh
now pre-creates both subdirs with 1001:1001 and 0755, matching the
parent. Fresh-install only — existing installs are unaffected (and
already work because of the 0777 mode that's still in place there).

### Upgrade notes

- Image swap only — no schema migrations, no manual steps.
- New audit actions show up immediately on the first enroll / restore
  / purge after the update. Existing audit rows are unchanged.
- The first-run.sh chown change runs only on fresh installs; existing
  deployments do not need to do anything.
- No customer-visible behavior change beyond richer audit trails.

# v0.1.22

Hotfix release. If you ran into "MQTT not connected" or "SFTP test failed" on the last step of the camera enrollment wizard — especially on a fresh install or after a factory reset — this is the release you want.

## What's fixed

### Camera enrollment now actually completes on first attempt

Three install-path bugs that turned a clean install into a multi-step manual recovery on v0.1.21:

- **SFTP "permission denied"** — `first-run.sh` provisioned the SFTPGo `camera` user (added in v0.1.21) but the home directory was created by a sibling service running as root, so SFTPGo itself couldn't write files into it. Install-time chown is now wired in; camera report uploads land on the first try.
- **MQTT silent TLS failure on re-installs** — the camera trust store check was matching certs by name only. Customers re-installing the stack onto an existing camera (which still had the prior install's CA cert) silently kept the old cert and TLS handshake failed against the new broker. Now the install computes a thumbprint and replaces a stale CA cleanly when names collide.
- **Inline-entered camera credentials weren't being saved** — operators who typed `admin` / password into the wizard rather than picking a stored credential ended up with a camera row in the DB that had no credential link. The wizard's MQTT/SFTP disable on delete then silently skipped because there were no credentials to authenticate to the camera with. Credentials entered inline are now persisted automatically.

### Camera-side cleanup when you remove a camera from the portal

Removing a camera from the portal now does a proper symmetric teardown on the camera itself:

1. Disables the camera's MQTT client (stops it talking to the broker)
2. Disables the four daily SFTP report uploads
3. Re-binds the MQTT TLS cert reference to the camera's default root cert
4. Removes our `AIDataCollect` CA from the camera's trust store

This keeps the camera in a clean state so a future re-enrollment — or a different stack install enrolling the same physical camera — doesn't trip the cert-name collision bug above.

If you Restore-within-24h, the symmetric restore step re-pushes the CA and re-binds MQTT, so a restored camera resumes traffic without any extra steps.

- **Connected sites** — Settings → System → Updates → Install all.
- **Closed-network sites** — download the `.adcupdate` bundle below and use Install from file.

If you're freshly installing from scratch (not upgrading), grab the latest `install.sh` from the deploy repo and run it. The SFTPGo and chown fixes only ship via `first-run.sh`, so a fresh install picks them up automatically.

# v0.1.21

## What's new

### Camera enrollment reliability (the big one)
Two longstanding bugs were causing the wizard to show **MQTT — not connected** and **SFTP — test failed** even when the camera was actually delivering data fine. Both are fixed:

- **MQTT status badge** now reads the camera's actual connection state. Previously the parser was looking at the wrong field name and silently treating every camera as "configured but not connected" regardless of what the camera reported. Wizards on newer Hanwha firmware (W9 family, e.g. XNV-A9084R) will now flip to a green dot the moment the camera connects.
- **SFTP probe poll window** was too tight (10s ceiling) and would call a slower camera as "not connected" even when the report upload was about to succeed a second later. Bumped to 18s so a slower-network camera still gets caught.

If you previously saw yellow/red dots on the last wizard step that didn't match reality, re-enroll the affected camera after upgrading and the badges should match what the camera is actually doing.

### Reports delivery now works on fresh installs
On a brand-new install, the SFTP server's user table was empty, so the first time a camera tried to deliver a report it would silently fail with "user not found." Reports would never arrive and nothing in the UI explained why. `first-run.sh` now provisions the camera user during install. Re-running `first-run.sh` is idempotent — it'll refresh the password rather than error out.

This affects new installs only. Existing sites where reports are already flowing are unaffected.

### Licensing
- **Identity_unreadable band** — when the license server can't read the host's stable identity (a transient OS issue, mid-update, etc.), the system now surfaces that explicitly in the License page instead of falling back to a generic "verification failed" message. Operators can tell at a glance whether the issue is the license itself or a host-side identity readback.
- **Capacity check fails closed** on a DB error. Previously a transient query failure would let enrollment slip through. Now it errs on the safe side and refuses enrollment until the DB is reachable again.
- **"Signed by" label** in the License page is now clearer that it refers to the advisory envelope, not the verified key — a small but important distinction when troubleshooting a license that's correctly signed but not yet trusted.
- **Fingerprint computed at most once per minute** under heavy reverify load — eliminates redundant kernel reads during every-tick license checks.

- **Connected sites** — Settings → System → Updates → Install all.
- **Closed-network sites** — download the `.adcupdate` bundle below and use Install from file.

## What's new

- **Smoother install confirmation dialogs.** When you click **Install all**, **Roll back**, or other update actions, the confirmation now appears as a styled dialog that matches the rest of the portal instead of the browser's default popup. This works the same regardless of your browser's dialog settings, and looks better in dark mode and on mobile.

- **Clearer per-action wording.** Each dialog now distinguishes between safe operations (regular install with backup) and riskier ones (skipping backup on stateful services, installing prerelease hotfixes) with color-coded buttons and an icon — warning amber for normal installs, danger red for actions that bypass safety nets.

- **Keyboard-friendly.** Press **Esc** to cancel or **Enter** to confirm — same as before, just on a properly themed dialog.

## Upgrade notes

No configuration changes. The change is purely how the confirmation dialogs render — the underlying install/rollback/restore logic is unchanged from v0.1.11.

v0.1.6 closes two errors that v0.1.5 lab verification surfaced post-wizard.

**api `0c06fe7` develop**:
- **#22** alerts.py:ensure_tables() ran CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX / ALTER TABLE on every /alerts/* request with zero locking. When the portal swapped to the dashboard right after wizard finalize, concurrent /alerts/?... and /alerts/hourly?... requests raced on pg_class_relname_nsp_index → transient 500s. Same class of race v0.1.3 closed for main schema-init via pg_advisory_xact_lock. Hoisted alerts DDL into _run_migrations; alerts.py:ensure_tables stays as idempotent defense-in-depth.
- **#23** cdp_v2_reprobe selected c.device_model — column was never defined in any schema. The error was masked pre-v0.1.5 by the camera_credentials UndefinedTableError on the same JOIN; v0.1.5 closed the table error, exposing this dead column reference. Dropped from query.

**api `028871a` develop** — closes three classes of fresh-install errors:

Also adds INFO start/end logging in `_run_migrations()` and a unit test guarding the hoisted DDL.

Recommended for every v0.1.3 install. Same compatibility envelope (`from: v0.1.0`).

v0.1.3 closes the v0.1.2 transient race window.

v0.1.2 used `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` + early return for the migration loser worker, but that loser then started its background services BEFORE the winner's migration transaction committed — producing a ~5s window of transient `UndefinedTable` errors in service logs + a single HTTP 500 on the first dashboard load.

**Fix (api `d330fbf` develop)**: switch to blocking `pg_advisory_xact_lock`. Loser waits for winner's COMMIT (which releases the xact-lock) before proceeding. By the time it starts services, schema is committed and visible. No more transient first-tick window.

Other repos in this release are no-op tag bumps. Recommended for any v0.1.2 fresh install that observed transient errors at boot. Same compatibility envelope as v0.1.2 (`from: v0.1.0`).

v0.1.2 hotfix release. Critical schema-init race fix plus 4 other install-path bugs caught in v0.1.1 lab smoke.

**Fixes:**
- **(#16, CRITICAL)** `aidatacollect-api`: schema-init race. Two uvicorn workers concurrently called `create_hypertable`, colliding on `pg_type_typname_nsp_index` and leaving the schema half-applied (missing tables: sites, zone_display_names; missing column: mqtt_transport). Fix: serialize `_run_migrations` with `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` + eager base-table creates + per-statement SAVEPOINTs.
- **(#17)** install-history.json chmod 0644 → 0666 so the api container can write the trial anti-cheat anchor on /setup/finalize.
- **(#13)** first-run.sh writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-aidatacollect-reserved-ports.conf reserving SFTPGo passive 60000-60010 from the kernel ephemeral pool (32768-60999) so `docker compose up` never races a transient ephemeral source port.
- **(#14)** install.sh + first-run.sh recovery panels print copy-pastable absolute paths + remind about `newgrp docker`.
- **(#15)** first-run.sh auto re-execs under `sg docker -c` when the user is in the docker group but the shell session predates the group add.
